missionPremise: Ruling 5 as amended by A-224 (_decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md, operator 2026-09-18 ~17:55Z): each of the 40 cities that carry no ruled setback table is classified FROM ITS OWN LAW into exactly one of (a) zoned, layer never acquired -> declared refusal naming the city; (b) unzoned, the ordinance sets a city-wide line -> default row with plat disclosure (Gholson first, OT-10); (c) unzoned, no city-wide line -> checked absence naming what was read. The premise has teeth because the setback writer releases only unaccounted cells: a cell written as refused, absent-verified or a value is permanent, so a city wrongly classed (b) freezes a fabricated line onto real parcels. A class is a claim about what a city's own ordinance says - never inferred from a search summary and never from a parcel carrying a district code. This lane owns the 19 cities the first lane (_inbox/2026-09-18_p300-p338-setback-residual-writer_city-classification.json) left unresolved or unexamined, on the first lane's own recommendation, and the writer build (P-300/P-338, separate dispatch) waits for this table.
completionPredicate: One row per city for the 19 cities, in the first lane's table shape, carrying the class (a/b/c) or unclassified, the ordinance section read, its URL, the date read, and a quote with the decisive text - with (b) rows carrying the line's values and (c) rows carrying what was read that sets no city-wide line, and every unclassifiable city named with what would settle it. Satisfied by _inbox/2026-09-19_p300-city-classification_table.json: 19/19 rows filed, 11 classified at source (2,331 parcels (a); 487 (b); 195 (c)), 8 unclassified by name with a single named action each (3,195 parcels). NOT satisfied in the sense of a complete classification: 51.5 percent of this lane's parcels still carry no class, which is why the status is closed-partial and not closed.
scopeBasis: The dispatch's own scope: the 19 cities with no ruled setback table that the first lane did not settle (6 unresolved + 13 unexamined), which is the residue of P-326's 40-city / 49,855-parcel population. Excluded deliberately: (1) the first lane's 20 (a) + 1 (b) cities - not re-read, only restated for the roll-up; (2) Woodcreek's 1,026 district-on-file parcels - out of P-300's population by P-326's own measurement because Woodcreek needs a real district table, not a jurisdiction default; (3) any district LIST for the (a) cities - the dispatch asks for a class, and a district table is the writer's artifact, not this lane's; (4) any store, code, corpus or deploy work - out of scope by the dispatch's constraint line.

LESSON: A code that omits a zoning chapter does not show a city is unzoned (Granger), and a city's presence in a code host's index does not show its code is served (Creedmoor on Municode). Both directions need a read, not an index.

For small Texas cities the city's own site inventory is the highest-yield path: Mountain City's and Creedmoor's zoning instruments were reachable in minutes from the city's own pages and were invisible to search summaries.
An absence claim (class c) needs completeness of the read in a way an existence claim (a/b) does not; write it only when the read covers the city's own ordinance set and say what the read covered.
